faq.question: How does the Webpage to Audio cost estimator work?
faq.answer: It converts a webpage's word count into characters, then multiplies by a TTS provider's per-character price. It also estimates audio duration using your chosen words-per-minute speech rate and shows monthly cost if you convert articles on a recurring schedule.

faq.question: How accurate is the word-to-character conversion?
faq.answer: We use 5.5 characters per word including spaces and punctuation, which is typical for clean English prose. Actual HTML pages include navigation, ads, and markup, so paste the clean article text or use a readability extractor for better accuracy.

faq.question: What speech speed should I pick?
faq.answer: Use 120 wpm for slow, accessible narration; 150 wpm for conversational content; 160 wpm for podcasts; and 180 wpm for fast narrators or speed-listening.

faq.question: Why do costs vary so much between providers?
faq.answer: TTS pricing ranges from free self-hosted models to premium cloned voices. Hyperscalers like Google, Amazon, and Azure charge roughly $16/1M characters for neural voices. ElevenLabs and premium tiers can be 3-6× more per character.

faq.question: Can I use this for newsletters or answer-engine content?
faq.answer: Yes. The tool is ideal for estimating the cost of turning blog posts, newsletter issues, and answer summaries into audio so you can budget for audio distribution or voice agents.
